fin.internationalNote: Santa Monica College F-1 international cost $25,658 (2026-27, Tier-1 verified from SMC's official International Student Tuition & Fees page for Fall 2026 - Summer 2027): non-resident tuition $486 a unit × 24 units = $11,664 + SMC health $56, Associated Students resource $20, student benefits $45 and student representation $4 = $125 in fees + SMC's published living-expenses allowance $13,869. NO credit-load assumption was needed — SMC states the basis itself (24 units across 2 semesters, the F-1 minimum of 12 a semester). ⚠ READ THE HOUSING LINE CAREFULLY: SMC has NO on-campus housing at all, so the $13,869 is NOT billed by the college — it is SMC's own 9-month living-expenses estimate based on a HOMESTAY WITH TWO MEALS A DAY, and SMC's page says a student with free room and board locally may deduct it in full. It is stored under `roomBoard` because a player still has to live somewhere and a tuition-only figure would badly understate the real outlay. Mandatory F-1 health insurance ($2,310) is excluded by convention, as are books ($1,064) and personal expenses ($4,968); SMC's own total for the year is $34,000. The previous stored $9,000 was an unresearched ballpark and understated the cost by $16,658 — nearly threefold, the largest PROPORTIONAL error in the campaign. As a CCCAA program Santa Monica cannot offer athletic scholarships at all, so this figure is very close to what is actually paid.

acuAlignNote: Murray State's Associate of Science in Health, Wellness & Human Performance is a genuine 2-year exercise-science transfer degree rather than a generic transfer A.A. Mapped against the college's own 2025-26 degree check sheet: AP 1113 Applied Anatomy covers ANAT100; BIO 1114 General Biology covers BIOL125; HWP 2963 Introduction to Kinesiology covers EXSC224 (mechanical bases of movement); HWP 1011 Strength and Conditioning covers EXSC216; and PSY 2213 Wellness, Exercise, and Sports Psychology covers both EXSC199 and EXSC296. The gap that matters most for Olivier: the degree contains no exercise-physiology course at all, so EXSC225 and EXSC322 — two of the four units WES is most likely to credit directly — are NOT covered here, and neither is research methods (EXSC122). The program core does add HWP 2713 Care and Prevention of Athletic Injuries and HWP 2213 First Aid, both useful pre-PT context. An Athletic Training Option of the same degree swaps in HWP 2972 Athletic Training Practicum, which would add supervised clinical hours in the EXSC398 mould — worth raising with the program chair if pre-PT is the goal. Confirm all equivalences with an MSC advisor and a formal WES evaluation before transfer planning.

The Support & Related Electives list — advisor-approved, not automatic — includes HPER 2623 Physiology of Exercise (a direct match for EXSC225) and both HPER 2643 Applied Anatomy and HSBC 2114 Human Anatomy (covering ANAT100); the 7-hour Sciences general-education requirement can also be satisfied with a BIOL-prefix course (BIOL125). No dedicated Strength & Conditioning or research-methods course was confirmed. Full WES evaluation and advisor confirmation required before relying on the elective-dependent units (EXSC225, ANAT100).

rec: Rose State stands apart from the rest of this batch on lifestyle and academics: Midwest City sits directly in the Oklahoma City metro, minutes from downtown, and the college offers the strongest ACU-relevant degree found among these four schools — a genuine Health & Sport Sciences A.S. with an Exercise/Fitness Management option including an actual Physiology of Exercise course. The honest trade-off is on-field form: two mid-table seasons (2024 4-7-1, 2025 5-5-2) with a first-round penalty-shootout exit in 2025 and no tournament breakthrough in the years reviewed. At $18,855/yr it sits mid-pack on cost, with on-campus housing (The Village at Rose State) available.
